jobs.title: Packaging Lead Engineer
jobs.description:
Packaging Lead Engineer

In this role you will be responsible for setting up the enterprise packaging strategy and technology roadmap while leading a group of engineers.

Develop, implement, and maintain comprehensive process standards and documentation to support all end-to-end packaging business and engineering workflows.

Establish packaging standards and lead execution of automation, returnable, and expendable plans while setting the standard on how Autoliv will achieve cost, quality, and sustainability goals. Assign workload to a team of engineers for new launch.

Should you be interested in overseeing these tasks and aiming for enhanced performance standards, your role will involve :

What you'll do

• Establish and maintain packaging standards for automation, returnable, and expendable execution; publish controlled specifications and playbooks

• Lead governance for exceptions/waivers; chair the standards review board and manage change control (ECO/ECN)

• Define common footprints and automation execution standards; align with safety/quality and sustainability requirements.

• Own enterprise packaging data architecture and tools (spec/PFEP, cartonization, labeling, image vaults): governance, permissions, and data-quality SLAs.

• Standardize master data (part-to-pack links, dunnage IDs, test results, sustainability attributes) and audit routines; lead training and adoption.

• Select/administer cartonization and labeling systems (GS1/AIAG compliant), including template libraries and formal change control.

• Set/enforce ID standards (serialization, barcode/QR/RFID), labeling, and traceability checkpoints (ship/receive scans, gate checks).

• Own the portfolio/roadmap for packaging materials, formats, and automation; prioritize pilots with success criteria and scale proven solutions.

• Conduct market/technology scouting; partner with suppliers/startups to mature innovations into standards.

• Develop KPIs/dashboards; monitor compliance and drive corrective actions with site leaders.

• Mentor regional teams; build capability via training, playbooks, and office hours

• Lead and set workload for a team of packaging engineers for new model launch and serialization projects

What is required

• BS in Packaging Engineering (preferred) or ME/IE

• 7–10+ years in packaging or logistics engineering, including multi-site standards/systems ownership in automotive/Tier-1 or similar high-volume manufacturing.

• Hands-on with PFEP/spec databases, cartonization (TOPS/Cape or WMS-native), labeling, and GS1/AIAG compliance.

• Experience integrating packaging data with ERP/PLM/WMS (e.g., SAP/Oracle; Teamcenter/Windchill); strong Excel/BI; familiarity with APIs/MDM concepts.

• Working knowledge of ISTA/ASTM transit testing, load-securement, and sustainability/EPR considerations.

• CAD & Packaging: SolidWorks/NX/CATIA; ArtiosCAD for corrugated/dunnage; read drawings, GD&T, basic tolerance stacks.

What’s in it for you

• Attractive compensation package

• Recognition awards, company events, family events, university discount options and many more perks.

• Gender Pay Equality

Equal opportunity employer

Autoliv is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. Autoliv does not discriminate in any aspect of employment based on race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, gender, sexual orientation, gender identify and/or expression, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local employment discrimination laws where Autoliv does business.

jobs.title: Packaging Engineer
jobs.description:
Sealed Air designs and delivers packaging solutions that protect essential goods transported worldwide, preserve food, enable e-commerce and digital connectivity, and help create a global supply chain that is touchless, safer, less wasteful, and more resilient. We strive to foster a caring, high-performance growth culture that will deliver consistent, sustainable profitable growth and accelerate our performance – a culture where accountability is clear and aligned, and where we reward business outcomes and impact. That culture guides everything we do, including how we partner with our customers and suppliers, how we attract and retain top talent, and how we create and deliver value to our stakeholders. In 2025, Sealed Air generated $5.4 billion in sales and has approximately 16,100 employees who serve customers in 119 countries/territories. To learn more, visit www.sealedair.com .

Job Description

Pay range: $81,900-$122,900 (The offered rate is depending on experience)
The range disclosed complies with applicable state and local pay transparency laws. Offers within this range will be determined by considering relevant factors including education, experience, and internal alignment.

Primary job responsibilities:

The individual will support Sealed Air Global Operations and Customers to ensure acceptable packaging materials are used. Focus will be on reducing damage in transit caused by inadequate packaging material and design, reducing cost by qualifying alternate packaging and suppliers, and achieve sustainability goals. The individual will work independently, and in conjunction with engineers, operational leaders, and production personnel both at Sealed Air factories, outsource partners, and customers.

Essential duties and responsibilities:

• Conduct Packaging trials, validate and qualify new Packaging Suppliers and Materials.

• Develop Packaging Shipping Standards and Specifications to prevent damage, reduce cost, and improve customer satisfaction.

• Design and implement alternate packages to meet various requirements for Quality, Cost or Sustainability

• Work in coordination with Region Sites to reduce package waste and increase packaging effectiveness with new materials.

• Partner with the sites and Sustainability coordinators to develop new methods to dispose of package waste, lowering cost and improving our Sustainability footprint.

• Investigate carrier management and claims administration to reduce in-transit damage. Identify and route-cause quality issues related to packaging failure and transit distribution. Assist with development of corrective and preventative actions.

• Study problems and use Operations Excellence Manufacturing tools to understand impact on organization. A systems approach should be taken to address end to end supply chain.

• Work with vendors (both approved and potential) and Purchasing to develop concepts and prototype containers and other packaging supplies

• Coordinate trials with logistics, quality, manufacturing, safety, scheduling and engineering to ensure transparency in validation.

• Create standard work instructions for packaging solutions to be rolled out throughout entire North American supply chain.

• Follow up and audit the implemented solution to ensure compliance.

• Create new material numbers and work to obsolete old, inactive materials.

• Generate Purchase Request in SAP for materials to conduct trials & pilot runs.

• Coordinate packaging requirements and specifications with external vendors to ensure standardization across Sealed Air operations.

• Provide resolution to packaging-related issues at Sealed Air manufacturing plants, and customers.

• Collaborate with Product Technology and R&D to establish packaging standards for new products.

• Support new packaging automation initiatives by ensuring packaging requirements are integrated into system designs and that quality standards are met.

• Identify and lead packaging changes for improved performance (reduce damaged in transit), cost savings, and sustainability

Qualifications

• Demonstrated flexibility within a high-performance work environment and matrix managed organization.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills along with professional presentation and negotiation skills.

• Bachelor of Science in Packaging Engineering, Packaging Science or related field.

• Requires experience with varied packaging processes and materials.

• Requires knowledge of statistical techniques and tools, their use and interpretation

• Requires ability to manage a project and process involving multiple manufacturing areas, plants, and across various portions of the business.

• Has demonstrated ability to work independently and focus on critical project parameters that determine success or failure.

• Design of Experiments, Lean Six Sigma, SPC or equivalent experience preferred.

• Self-starter capable of working independently with minimal supervision.

• Relevant professional experience preferred.

• Travel up to 10%.

Safety Requirements:

• Works around rotating equipment, hot polymers, and high noise environments.

• Required to wear safety shoes as well as standard PPE.

• Exposed to various chemicals throughout the site.

• Comply with all established facility safety rules and policies.

• Comply with SQF policies throughout all facilities

jobs.title: Principal Project Engineer Blending & Packaging Vivid
jobs.description:
We are Reckitt

Home to the world's best loved and trusted hygiene, health, and nutrition brands. Our purpose defines why we exist: to protect, heal and nurture in the relentless pursuit of a cleaner, healthier world. We are a global team united by this purpose.
Join us in our fight to make access to the highest quality hygiene, wellness, and nourishment a right and not a privilege.

Supply

Our supply chain is the backbone of our business. It's how we get our trusted products to people all over the world, safely and efficiently. And it's our talented and passionate teams that make this happen.

If you're looking for a career in supply chain, there's no better place to be than Reckitt. We offer a variety of exciting opportunities in all areas of the supply chain, from planning and procurement to manufacturing and logistics. You could join our Global Supply Planning team to develop and implement our global supply strategy, or work with our Procurement Centre of Excellence team to negotiate and manage our supplier relationships.

Our Manufacturing Excellence team help us improve the efficiency, quality and safety of our manufacturing operations, and our Logistics Excellence team develop new and innovative ways to distribute our products to customers.

About the role

The Principal Project Engineer, Blending & Packaging is responsible for planning, designing, and overseeing the packaging projects for a large-scale supply chain transformation program in Zeeland, MI (Project Vivid). The packaging scope is part of a multi-story manufacturing plant, warehouse, offices, employee amenities, laboratories, and related scope such as roads and parking. This role involves ensuring that packaging projects are completed on time, within budget, and to the required quality standards. The Packaging Project Engineer works closely with other engineers, contractors, and stakeholders to deliver successful solutions.

Your responsibilities

• Lead the design, development, and execution of packaging and blending solutions for new assets while ensuring designs meet required regulatory, safety, environmental, and industry standards.

• Lead initiatives to optimize packaging materials, focusing on recyclability, reusability, and reduction of waste.

• Provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior engineers and cross-functional teams.

• Work closely with Project teams and cross functional teams (R&D, Marketing, Supply Chain, and Manufacturing) to align packaging with overall business objectives and ensure seamless integration into production.

• Responsibilities may include documentation management and an understanding of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs) as well of implementation of FDA standards.

• Creation and management of change requests within the document control system.

• Responsible for the success of the packaging execution projects, including but not limited to the commissioning and validation of it.

• Project Planning: Develop detailed project plans, including timelines, budgets, and resource allocation.

• Design and Analysis: Lead option analysis and packaging planning efforts. Work in partnership with engineering and construction partner firms to execute all phases of execution including commissioning.

• Quality Assurance: Conduct inspections and quality control checks to ensure the integrity and durability of packaging projects.

• Risk Management: Identify and mitigate potential risks associated with packaging projects.

• Project Reporting:

• Prepare and deliver project status presentations to senior leadership, executive stakeholders, and cross-functional teams.

• Communicate project progress, milestones, key performance indicators (KPIs), risks, and mitigation plans in a clear and concise manner.

• Provide regular updates on project scope, schedule, budget, and resource utilization to support informed decision-making.

• Develop presentation materials that summarize technical and operational information for diverse audiences.

• Lead project review meetings and facilitate discussions regarding priorities, challenges, and strategic direction.

• Translate complex project data into actionable insights and recommendations for leadership teams.

• Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities for process improvements and implement best practices in packaging engineering.

The experience we're looking for

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Packaging Engineering or related field.

• Experience: Minimum of 7 years of experience in packaging engineering in an FDA-regulated environment.

• Standards: Understanding of FDA, GMP, ASTM, and ISO guidelines.

• Skills:

• • Strong leadership, project management, and organizational skills.

• Proficiency in engineering software and tools (e.g., Revit, Autodesk Construction Cloud, Procore, AutoCAD, Civil 3D).

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.

• Knowledge of building design and construction methods, materials, and regulations.

• Technical Expertise: Deep understanding of packaging engineering principles and practices.

• Collaboration: Works effectively with cross-functional teams and stakeholders.

• Attention to Detail: Ensures accuracy and thoroughness in all project-related activities.

• Adaptability: Flexible and able to adapt to changing project requirements and priorities.

The skills for success

Supply Chain Management, Business Partnership, Collaboration and partnership building, Relationship Management, Business accumen, Productivity management, Improve business processes, Advanced Analytics, Data Analytics, Supply Chain Planning, Logistics Management.

What we offer

With inclusion at the heart of everything we do, working alongside our four global Employee Resource Groups, we support our people at every step of their career journey, helping them to succeed in their own individual way.

We invest in the wellbeing of our people through parental benefits, an Employee Assistance Program to promote mental health, and life insurance for all employees globally. We have a range of other benefits in line with the local market. Through our global share plans we offer the opportunity to save and share in Reckitt's potential future successes. For eligible roles, we also offer short-term incentives to recognise, appreciate and reward your work for delivering outstanding results. You will be rewarded in line with Reckitt's pay for performance philosophy.

Salary range

USD $119,200.00 - $178,800.00

Pay transparency

The base salary range for this role will vary based on experience in job and industry, training and education, skills relevant to the position, and other factors permitted by law. In addition to the base salary, the position is eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, which is subject to change each year.

Reckitt offers eligible employees competitive benefits including medical, prescription, dental, vision, and life and disability insurance; paid time off for vacation, sick and Company recognized holidays; a 401(k) plan; 16-week paid parental leave or 26 weeks for the birthing parent; adoption and fertility support; tuition reimbursement; discounts; and much more. Our compensation and benefits packages aim to give our talent the reward, protection, and peace of mind they deserve.

If reasonable accommodation is needed to complete your application, please contact NAtalentacquisition@reckitt.com. Reckitt is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals.

Equality

We recognise that in real life, great people don't always 'tick all the boxes'. That's why we hire for potential as well as experience. Even if you don't meet every point on the job description, if this role and our company feels like a good fit for you, we still want to hear from you.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, disability or medical condition; colour, ethnicity, race, citizenship, and national origin; religion, faith; pregnancy, family status and caring responsibilities; sexual orientation; sex, gender identity, gender expression, and transgender identity; protected veteran status; size or any other basis protected by appropriate law.

jobs.title: Packaging Engineer, Leo Customer Terminals
jobs.description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

As a Packaging Engineer, you will be responsible for working with US and regional teams, closely monitoring and driving packaging engineering initiatives and processes from concept through mass production. You will be an integral part of executing packaging build strategies, including DFM innovation, new product development, execution efficiency, and best practice. You will be a critical escalation path for packaging process issues and work closely with China and US leadership teams to ensure cross-functional collaboration is effective.

Export Control Requirement:
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, analyze, and document consumer-facing packaging components and assemblies that delight consumers at the lowest cost of ownership. Redefine what sustainable packaging can be.
- Conduct tests and engineering studies to validate the robustness and proper performance of new packaging. Identify and reduce packaging risks.
- Review and develop process, automation opportunities, and fixtures with contract manufacturers and packaging suppliers.
- Bring clarity, and simplicity to complexity, probe assumptions, illuminate pitfalls, and foster shared understanding of packages and their related processes.
- Travel domestically and internationally to supplier sites to collaborate with staff and keep teams moving.

A day in the life
In a given day, you will:

- Design, analyze, and document consumer-facing packaging components and assemblies that delight consumers at the lowest cost of ownership. Redefine what sustainable packaging can be.
- Conduct tests and engineering studies to validate the robustness and proper performance of new packaging. Identify and reduce packaging risks.
- Review and develop process, automation opportunities, and fixtures with contract manufacturers and packaging suppliers.
- Bring clarity, and simplicity to complexity, probe assumptions, illuminate pitfalls, and foster shared understanding of packages and their related processes, balancing tradeoffs such as cost, size, and schedule.
- Travel domestically and internationally to supplier sites to collaborate with staff and keep teams moving.

About the team
Amazon Leo is an initiative to increase global broadband access through a constellation of satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO). Its mission is to bring fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities around the world. Amazon Leo will help close the digital divide by delivering fast, affordable broadband to a wide range of customers, including consumers, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in places without reliable connectivity.

jobs.title: System Development Engineer, Robotics Delivery & Packaging Innovation (RDPI), RDPI Hardware Solutions
jobs.description:
Robotics Delivery & Packaging Innovation (RDPI) Global Engineering is looking for a System Development Engineer (SysDE) to join our New Product Introduction (NPI) team. Our mission is to eliminate operational complexity at the source, ensuring every RDPI automation solution is designed for deployability, reliability, and maintainability from Day One.

As a SysDE II on the NPI team, you will work alongside Hardware Development programs from the Alpha phase to help shape controls and system design before solutions are built. Rather than fixing deployment and reliability problems in the field, you will help design them out — contributing to the automation, firmware, and integration decisions that determine how easily a solution scales across our global network. You are a builder who designs and delivers the controls software and tooling for the systems you support, works autonomously on well-scoped problems while seeking direction on ambiguous ones, and partners with Hardware Development, Technical Program Managers, and the Scale and AI teams to deliver solutions that deploy with minimal human intervention.

This role is a strong fit for an engineer who thinks software-first and wants to grow in the software development craft. You will deepen core software engineering practices — modern languages, testing, CI/CD, and AI-native, agentic development — and apply them to industrial controls and hardware domains.

Key job responsibilities
- Contribute to NPI programs from Alpha through GA, helping influence controls and system design for deployability, reliability, and maintainability.
- Design and deliver standardized hardware/software interfaces and modular, reusable control patterns that reduce integration complexity, with guidance on the most ambiguous architectural decisions.
- Build and validate automation and commissioning frameworks (CI/CD for controls code, automated configuration validation, emulators) in partnership with the Scale team.
- Participate in reviews of architecture, design, and operations for your solutions, and incorporate feedback to raise the quality of your work.
- Partner with Hardware Development, TPMs, and the AI team to incorporate self-service deployment and predictive capabilities into solutions.
- Use AI-assisted and agentic development tools to increase the quality and velocity of your engineering work, and share what you learn with the team.
- Apply and help improve engineering and operational excellence standards, and mentor interns and junior engineers as you grow.

A day in the life
You work across industrial control platforms (Codesys, Allen-Bradley, Siemens, Beckhoff) and the networked field devices, firmware, and cloud/WMS interfaces around them. You design and build the controls software for a solution, contribute reusable control patterns to our libraries, write and review structured-text and automation-tooling code, and work with Hardware to improve a system before it's built. You take part in design reviews that surface architectural and scalability risks early, and you prototype frameworks, emulators, automated validation, and CI/CD for controls code that become the foundation future solutions are built on. You lean on AI and agentic development tools throughout — generating, testing, and troubleshooting code — so you can focus your judgment on building solutions that are correct by design.
